title: Judge Lab — architecture phase testset
purpose: Portable candidate evaluation tests for architecture and implementation of the deterministic judging app.

scope.includes: All 207 expansion scenarios, including the latest 35 policy revisions and three aligned boundary controls.
scope.excludes: The original 100 scenarios already in the existing questionnaire/testset.

import_contract.existing_ids: Update matching IDs; do not append duplicate copies. Preserve unrelated tests.
import_contract.gold_promotion: Preserve each validation status. Human source and outcome review is required before marking a candidate as gold.
import_contract.execution: Input and expected objects are evaluation fixtures, not executable CR code or a completed deterministic engine.
import_contract.settings: The TO settings are an application contract. The current questionnaire provides a local review preview, not a production tournament-settings backend.
import_contract.mode_evaluation: For tests with expected.integrity_policy, run both available_integrity_settings. The base expected.disposition uses the default setting; apply stage-specific expectations and the integrity workflow for other settings.
import_contract.visibility: This owner/developer bundle contains protected handoff reasons. Never expose the whole expected object, protected hypotheses, or source analysis as player-facing output.

modes.presume_good_faith: Apply ordinary rules and penalties under a rebuttable good-faith presumption.
modes.request_table_confirmation: Invite table confirmation of the reported account and good-faith explanation; record reports, not a vote or proof of innocence.

categories.PERMITTED_OR_NOT_RELEVANT: No integrity assumption is needed for the tested conduct or rule.
categories.ORDINARY_ERROR: Good-faith handling by default; perform necessary factual checks.
categories.STRONG_INDICATORS: Mandatory protected human review; no finding of guilt.

not_strong_by_itself: Refusal or disagreement by another player
Not reminding an opponent of their trigger
integrity_settings.player_prompt: Can the other players confirm the described sequence, or add any specific facts we have missed?
integrity_settings.source_kind: Owner-approved application workflow; does not change normative rules or penalties.

integrity_workflow_contract.full_backup: Always HANDOFF_TO_HUMAN; never execute a full backup.
integrity_workflow_contract.strong_indicators: HANDOFF_TO_HUMAN in both modes; table support cannot override. Referral does not determine guilt.
integrity_workflow_contract.missing_facts: Request the necessary facts; a good-faith presumption cannot supply missing facts.
integrity_workflow_contract.permitted_conduct: No integrity confirmation required for permitted non-reminding of an opponent’s trigger.
integrity_workflow_contract.ordinary_error_default: Apply ordinary rules and penalties under a rebuttable working presumption of good faith.

ordinary_error_table_mode.declined: Apply the ordinary ruling without treating refusal as guilt.
ordinary_error_table_mode.disagrees: CLARIFY_SPECIFIC_FACTS; disagreement alone is not strong evidence.

integrity_workflow_contract.stage_exception: POL-051 priority_pass_only is permitted; completed self-Chalice-checking invokes mandatory review.
integrity_workflow_contract.neutral_handoff_message: Please pause the game and call a human Judge. Keep the current game state unchanged until they arrive.

provenance.rules_and_oracle_versions: Retained per test; these are the source versions of the reviewed draft, not a claim that the sources will remain current.

input.player_message: Alice controls Dark Depths with no ice counters. Its sacrifice ability is on the stack. Bob casts Stifle targeting that ability; Stifle resolves. Dark Depths is still on the battlefield with no ice counters. Has Bob stopped Marit Lage permanently? What happens next?
assumptions: No unmentioned effects change the stated interaction.
The stated resolutions occur only after the required priority passes.
input.fact_provenance: Facts in the scenario are stipulated for this test. Player quotations remain reported claims; no real-world observations are asserted.

expected.ruling: No. Dark Depths triggers again after the countered ability leaves the stack.
intermediate_propositions: This is a state trigger, not a state-based action and not a trigger only for removing the last counter.
It cannot trigger again while its ability is on the stack.
After Stifle counters that ability, the condition is still true, so it triggers again and is put on the stack at the next opportunity.

source_proposition_consequence.proposition: This is a state trigger, not a state-based action and not a trigger only for removing the last counter. It cannot trigger again while its ability is on the stack. After Stifle counters that ability, the condition is still true, so it triggers again and is put on the stack at the next opportunity.
source_proposition_consequence.consequence: No. Dark Depths triggers again after the countered ability leaves the stack.

checks: Preserve decision-critical timing and actor identities.
Match the expected disposition and material result, allowing equivalent wording.
Support the material intermediate propositions with the cited current source provisions.
Do not say Stifle removes the ability from the land.
Do not label the trigger a state-based action.

Zero is less than one, so its win condition is not met.

source_proposition_consequence.consequence: No. The trigger resolves with devotion zero and a one-card library.

Paying life for a Phyrexian symbol or using delve does not change mana value.
Misstep itself has mana value 1, but a spell on the stack cannot target itself.
Vampiric Tutor remains the only legal target.
Swat allows Alice to leave the original target unchanged; she is not required to invent a different target.
Swat then goes to the graveyard.
The other spells remain on the stack; Misstep does not resolve as part of Swat's resolution.

input.player_message: Competitive REL Legacy. Alice chose Human for Cavern of Souls. She casts Snapcaster Mage, tapping an Island and Cavern to pay its {1}{U} cost. She does not announce which Cavern mana ability she used or say that the spell cannot be countered. Bob casts Force of Will targeting Snapcaster Mage and argues that Alice never explicitly chose Cavern's colored-mana ability. Neither player previously specified the colorless ability or a different shortcut. What is the ruling?
assumptions: Apply only the expressly stated REL and event policy.
Do not infer intent from an error.
input.fact_provenance: Facts in the scenario are stipulated for this test. Player quotations remain reported claims; no real-world observations are asserted.

expected.ruling: Apply the MTR 4.2 shortcut: Alice is assumed to have activated Cavern's colored-mana ability. Snapcaster Mage cannot be countered by Force of Will.
intermediate_propositions: When an object has multiple mana abilities, the tournament shortcut assumes the one most specifically applicable to the spell or ability being paid for, unless the player announces otherwise.
Cavern's restricted colored-mana ability specifically applies to this Human creature spell.

Alice need not recite the ability or announce 'uncounterable'.
Force of Will has a legal target but does not counter it.
